content.text: I have all the info I need. Now I'll compile the structured output.

input.area: Reading footer pills — LikeButton and SaveButton in the story/chapter reader.
components: LikeButton (default export from components/LikeButton.tsx) — pill button with inline Heart SVG, optimistic like toggle, count display

SaveButton (default export from components/SaveButton.tsx) — pill button with inline BookmarkIcon SVG, optimistic save toggle, label Save/Saved; anonymous users get a Link to /signup instead of a button
input.currentBehavior:
LikeButton already has a GSAP scaffold: imports gsap, prefersReducedMotion, useGSAP from @/lib/gsap, a buttonRef on the <button>, and a useGSAP scope wrapping the ref. It defines a `pulse()` helper that does `gsap.fromTo(buttonRef.current, { scale: 1 }, { scale: 1.15, duration: 0.1, yoyo: true, repeat: 1, ease: 'power2.out' })`, gated on prefersReducedMotion(). `pulse()` is invoked at the top of `toggle()` (the onClick handler) before the optimistic state mutation. CSS-side, the .button has only `transition: color/background/border-color var(--transition-fast)` — no scale/transform transition; the .liked class swaps color/border/background to the --like family. The Heart SVG has its own `transition: fill var(--transition-fast)` on .icon.

SaveButton has NO animation today: no gsap import, no ref, no pulse. The onClick is `() => void toggle()`; `toggle()` flips `saved` optimistically, calls postSave/deleteSave, and rolls back on non-409 errors. CSS-side, .button transitions color/border-color/background only; the .saved class swaps to --gold / --gold-dim. The BookmarkIcon has no transition.

Both components disable the button while `pending` is true (SaveButton also disables until `hydrated`). The anonymous SaveButton renders an <a> (Next Link) with no click handler at all — animation should be skipped there.
input.integrationPoints:
Target element for both: the <button ref={buttonRef}> root (the pill). Hook the animation into the existing onClick path — specifically, inside the `toggle` function before the optimistic state mutation (same spot LikeButton already calls `pulse()`).

LikeButton: extend the existing `pulse()` (LikeButton.tsx lines 47-55) — already called on line 59 inside `toggle`. Use `var(--like)` (e.g., #e07b7b) for the click-feedback color (flash/glow/ring). Keep the prefersReducedMotion() guard.

SaveButton: needs the full scaffold added — (1) `import { gsap, prefersReducedMotion, useGSAP } from '@/lib/gsap'`, (2) `const buttonRef = useRef<HTMLButtonElement>(null)` and attach to the authenticated <button> on line 97, (3) a useGSAP({ scope: buttonRef }) for cleanup, (4) a `pulse()` mirroring LikeButton's, and (5) call it at the top of `toggle` (before line 74's `const wasSaved = saved`). Use `var(--gold)` (e.g., #bf9b5e) for the click-feedback color. Do NOT animate the anonymous Link variant (lines 58-70) — keep it purely a navigation link.

Both: respect the existing `disabled` short-circuit (`if (pending) return`) so the pulse only fires when the click will actually run. Read CSS vars at runtime via `getComputedStyle(buttonRef.current).getPropertyValue('--like' | '--gold')` if the animation needs the color value (theme-aware: --like and --gold are redefined for dark and high-contrast themes).
input.notes:
Per-button colors are already defined as CSS custom properties in app/globals.css and used by the existing active states:

  - LikeButton active color: --like (#e07b7b light / #d97070 dark / #b5483f high-contrast) and --like-tint (rgba alpha bg). Used by .liked in LikeButton.module.css line 40-49 and by .iconFilled (fill+stroke).
  - SaveButton active color: --gold (#bf9b5e light / #c9a26a dark / #8a6a2e high-contrast) and --gold-dim (rgba alpha bg). Used by .saved in SaveButton.module.css line 36-47.

Use those vars so the click-flash automatically follows the theme; don't hardcode hex. Other shared design tokens in play: --bg-surface, --border-line, --border-line-hover, --text, --text-muted, --radius-pill, --transition-fast, --font-ui, --fs-tag, --tracking-tag.

GSAP is centralized in lib/gsap.ts — always import gsap/useGSAP/prefersReducedMotion from '@/lib/gsap', never directly from 'gsap'. ScrollTrigger is auto-registered there. prefersReducedMotion() should gate any motion (LikeButton already does this; SaveButton must follow the same pattern).

LikeButton is consumed by app/story/[id]/page.tsx and app/chapter/[id]/page.tsx; SaveButton is consumed by the same two pages. Both buttons sit side-by-side in the reading footer pill row alongside Share, so the click feedback should stay subtle/scale-based to keep that row visually consistent.

framework note (per frontend/AGENTS.md): this Next.js may diverge from training data — both components are already "use client" with the correct hook setup, so no app-router server-component pitfalls to worry about here.
